blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Central Information Commission (CIC) has the duty to receive and inquire into complaints from any person unable to submit an RTI request or refused information.
While inquiring into any matter, the CIC holds the powers of a Civil Court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.
During an inquiry, no public record may be withheld from the Commission on any grounds.
The CIC can order public authorities to secure compliance with the RTI Act, including appointing PIOs, publishing information, and paying compensation.
The Commission submits an annual report to the Central Government, which is subsequently laid before both Houses of Parliament.

items: CIC is a Statutory Body created under the Right to Information Act, 2005, and NOT a Constitutional Body.
The decisions of the Commission are final and binding, though subject to judicial review by High Courts and the Supreme Court under writ jurisdiction.
The maximum penalty that CIC can impose on an officer for delaying or refusing information is ₹250 per day, up to a maximum limit of ₹25,000.
